interpretation: Longer uninterrupted local Thalassia occupancy history predicts re-recording after a one-year exact-point loss even after stable transect identity, loss year, loss-year vegetation state, and source mixed-species state are controlled. This supports a local legacy/residual-structure signal beyond broad node quality and immediate community continuity.
ecological_boundary: The historical-state signal is consistent with residual rhizomes/clonal persistence or persistent microsite quality, but the monitoring data cannot distinguish those mechanisms from repeated detectability without direct below-ground measurements.
claim_boundary: Post-hoc exploratory exact-point temporal ecology on an already-opened recovery endpoint.
Do not call the run-length effect direct evidence of clonal memory, residual rhizomes, or facilitation.
Return is recorded reappearance at the same meter mark, not proven genet-level recolonization.
The exposure remains continuous; no outcome-driven streak threshold is authorized.
Stable-node and community-state controls reduce but do not eliminate unmeasured microsite habitat or observation persistence.
